notes.title: Dev Diary #30 - Build Update Progress
notes.notes:
Hi all! 


# Progress Report


Now that public playtesting is concluded, I've been working doubly hard on getting various issues sorted out across the game as well as starting on remaining features on the to-do list! I'm hoping to have a better idea of a release schedule in the near future. I'm also trying to decide if something like Early Access makes sense in this case as the bulk of the game nears completion. I'd be happy to hear any feedback! 



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43607312/1a42ef859e42aefec1a9f18678095928bafd4603.jpg"]


## Release notes:


Feature: Added "teamwork" trait for certain skill sets



Enhancement: When traveling, the POI detector UI will show direction as well as distance

Enhancement: When traveling, the POI detector UI will indicate if the POI is known or not

Enhancement: Update backstories, traits, and skill set flavor texts

Enhancement: Backstories and skill sets both influence starting money and reputation

Enhancement: Update save file format (JSON rather than a binary format)

Enhancement: Update event director logic

Enhancement: Travel manager will add the starting location to the codex on starting a new journey

Enhancement: Event popups will show when items are removed from inventory



Fix: Map position indicator stayed visible after switching scenes with map open

Fix: Minor cleanup issues in certain classes

Fix: Minor issues in main menu UI

Fix: Remove redundant save game calls

Fix: Event director wasn't respecting minimum cells between random events

Fix: Travel scenery scrolling was affected by changes to travel speed button options

Fix: Minor typo in starting dialog grammar

Fix: Various issues with main menu > new game flow, especially with the back button

Fix: Character creation UI wasn't being reset after creating a character

Fix: Initialization of codex pages in journal was incomplete, showing placeholder text instead

Fix: Journal showed object name rather than location name in status text

Fix: Injury events weren't removing medical items selected for use from inventory

Fix: Injury events weren't notifying such that popups would show on travel screen



Change: Adjust base POI detector distance

Change: Tweak the traits that each backstory and skill set have

Change: Adjust UI layout when selecting a skill set

Change: Lower the volume of all typewriter effects

Change: When traveling, the POI detector UI will hide if on the same map cell

Change: Journal won't show biome/weather conditions if the journey hasn't begun yet

Change: Disabled certain items from showing in the game until they are fully implemented

notes.title: Dev Diary #28 - Build & Playtesting Update
notes.notes:
Hi all! 


# Progress Report


In the last couple of weeks, there has been quite a bit of activity with Journey Express! 

First of all thank you for everyone that has tried out the Playtest -- I really appreciate the interest! Please see the notes down below about the playtest's duration, as it will soon be deactivated!

Secondly, quite a few changes have been made all around the game to make things work better, be more intuitive, and lay the groundwork for future development!


# Playtesting

## Release notes:


Fix a number of various issues with the UI in the journal

Show party member hunger level in the status screen

Add way to detecting locations and discoveries while traveling

Generate nav-meshes for AI agents in the exploration scenes

Set coordinates of discoveries so they are correctly positioned on the map

Fix some incorrect sprites for items/traits

Add traveling salesman event

Fix some issues with travel scenery

Add credits to main menu


## Playtest Signups


Like I mentioned last time, if you're interested at all in playtesting Journey Express, feel free to request access via the green button on the store page!



Note that the Playtest will be ending soon! I plan to deactivate the playtesting feature for Journey Express on Sunday (August 31st)! 



Thank you for your interest and feedback!

notes.title: Dev Diary #20 - Bug Fixes, Boons & Banes
notes.notes:
Hi all!

It has been a minute since the last update, but I'm working on getting things moving faster again!


 FIX: There were a number of minor bugs that cascaded into a bigger overall problem with the in-game event resolution system. When a random event occurs, things should actually take effect when the player responds to it.
 FIX: A couple in-game events had mismatched event effects and conditions.
 CHANGE: Show each party member's last name in addition to their first name in the journal
 NEW FEATURE (WIP): I'm adding a new system for buffing or de-buffing the player's party overall for a given amount of time. The effects can for now either boost or reduce health and/or morale! For example, the Clear Weather event slightly raises the party's health and morale for a short period of time.
 OTHER: I'm continuing to work on end game functionality like different UI screens and implementation


I have since moved on to Bluesky for all social media updates! Feel free to follow me there! :)
https://bsky.app/profile/starcatgames.ltd


Thanks for reading!
- C

notes.title: Dev Diary #19 - A Bunch of Changes!
notes.notes:
Hi all!


 COMPLETED: The fishing mini-game is now what I consider "complete"! I'll no doubt make some changes to it in the future, but it'll do the job for now. There are currently 3 obstacle layouts where you launch a ball in an attempt to land it in the catcher at the bottom, which randomly positions itself when you start. I'll add more variety in future updates!
 NEW FEATURE: I've added new achievements for traveling the various biomes across the world map!
 NEW FEATURE: Food consumption! While I still need to add and test values for different food items, party members should now eat food while traveling to stay healthy (and happy)!
 IN-PROGRESS: Work continues on the travel logic concerning health and treatment tracking. Being able to easily tell the state of your party members is important, and I need to polish that aspect up yet.

notes.title: Dev Diary #11 - Unity Engine Update & Steam Rich Presence
notes.notes:
Hi all!

Unity Engine Update

I finally sorted out the issues I was having with various shaders, assets, and what not in getting Unity updated. The game is now running on version 2022.3, up from 2020.3. Getting weather effects, various materials, water shading, and camera stacking all working was something of a nightmare, but it seems to all be happy again. The benefit here is that the game isn't stuck years in the past as far as the engine goes, gaining any and all bug fixes, performance improvements, etc. Some of the assets I'm using have stopped supporting Unity 2020 so it was getting to the point where it was becoming an issue.

Steam Rich Presence

A new feature is integration with Steam Rich Presence, so you/your friends will be able to see what's going on with via your Steam status when playing:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43607312/cd5e8cc6e41a699f8a0f2398675f8fd8039c84cc.png

And finally, I've made some improvements to the build automation tools I'm using so it's easier to track build changes going forward.

Thanks!
- C

notes.title: Dev Diary #01 - Tile Inventory System, Bug Fixes & Steam Integration
notes.notes:
Hi all!

This week was mostly bug-fixing & cleaning up things here and there. Up next I think I'll tackle some of the UI for viewing and managing party health, such as treatments for injuries and sicknesses.

I first wrote the tile-based inventory for the exploration side of the game over a year ago, and have been putting off fixing some long-standing bugs. Namely issues with rotating asymmetrical items like the rifle shown below (4x1). Luckily most of the issues I had were easy enough to fix once I dug into it.

The core concept is that you can bring items with you from your party's inventory when you go exploring. For example, you could bring a rifle and ammo along for hunting. On the other side of the coin is being able to bring things back with you when you're done. Collecting things like meat, plants, fish, and valuables will help keep your journey moving smoothly.

The limit to what you can carry will be determined by two things: your weight capacity, and what you can fit on your person via the tiles. Certain tile zones will only allow certain types of items. Such as in the image below, the rifle will only be allowed to be carried in the backpack or shoulder tiles, and only small items can fit in the pockets.

A to-do item is to visually indicate where items can be dropped while dragging them so it's not just a guessing game.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43607312/627fcac2b64b58029f0a868db3070079169f6e61.gif

The other semi-major change is finally getting an implementation of hooking into Steam's API, mostly for achievements, but also just to get events and info from Steam.

That's all I've got this time around, thanks for reading!

- C
